slides.title: Introduction to Unsupervised Learning
slides.content:
# Unsupervised Learning 🔍

Discover hidden patterns without labels!

## What you'll learn:
- **Clustering** - Group similar data points
- **Dimensionality Reduction** - Simplify complex data
- **Anomaly Detection** - Find outliers

## Unsupervised vs Supervised

```
Supervised:
X = [[...], [...]]  # Features
y = [1, 0, 1, ...]  # Labels (have answers!)

Unsupervised:
X = [[...], [...]]  # Features only
# No labels - find patterns yourself!
```

## Use Cases

| Task | Application |
|------|-------------|
| Clustering | Customer segmentation |
| Dimensionality Reduction | Visualization, feature reduction |
| Anomaly Detection | Fraud detection, defect detection |

> 💡 **Unsupervised learning finds structure** in data without being told what to look for!

slides.title: Clustering - K-Means
slides.content:
# K-Means Clustering 📊

Group data into K clusters!

## How It Works

```
1. Choose K (number of clusters)
2. Initialize K centroids randomly
3. Assign each point to nearest centroid
4. Move centroids to cluster means
5. Repeat 3-4 until convergence
```

## Implementation

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# Create and fit model
kmeans = KMeans(
    n_clusters=3,      # Number of clusters
    random_state=42,
    n_init=10          # Number of initializations
)
kmeans.fit(X)

# Get cluster assignments
labels = kmeans.labels_

# Predict for new data
new_labels = kmeans.predict(new_X)

# Cluster centers
centers = kmeans.cluster_centers_
```

## Finding Optimal K (Elbow Method)

```python
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

inertias = []
for k in range(2, 11):
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42)
    kmeans.fit(X)
    inertias.append(kmeans.inertia_)

# Plot inertias - look for "elbow" point
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(range(2, 11), inertias, 'bo-')
plt.xlabel('Number of clusters')
plt.ylabel('Inertia')
plt.show()
```

> 💡 **The "elbow" is where adding more clusters stops helping much!**

slides.title: Other Clustering Methods
slides.content:
# More Clustering Algorithms 🎯

## Hierarchical Clustering

```python
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

model = AgglomerativeClustering(
    n_clusters=3,
    linkage='ward'  # 'average', 'complete', 'single'
)
labels = model.fit_predict(X)
```

## DBSCAN (Density-Based)

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

model = DBSCAN(
    eps=0.5,         # Maximum distance between points
    min_samples=5    # Minimum points to form cluster
)
labels = model.fit_predict(X)

# -1 means noise/outlier!
```

## When to Use Which?

| Algorithm | Best For |
|-----------|----------|
| K-Means | Large datasets, spherical clusters |
| Hierarchical | Small datasets, want dendrogram |
| DBSCAN | Arbitrary shapes, outlier detection |

## Evaluating Clusters

```python
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

score = silhouette_score(X, labels)
# Range: -1 to 1, higher is better
# > 0.5 is good, > 0.7 is excellent
```

> 🎯 **DBSCAN is great for outlier detection** - points labeled -1 are anomalies!

slides.title: Dimensionality Reduction - PCA
slides.content:
# PCA - Principal Component Analysis 📉

Reduce dimensions while keeping important information!

## Why Reduce Dimensions?

- 🚀 **Faster training** - Fewer features
- 📊 **Visualization** - Plot in 2D or 3D
- 🧹 **Remove noise** - Focus on signal
- 🔧 **Avoid curse of dimensionality**

## How PCA Works

```
1. Center the data (subtract mean)
2. Find directions of maximum variance
3. Project data onto top N directions
```

## Implementation

```python
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# Reduce to 2 dimensions
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_reduced = pca.fit_transform(X)

# Or keep 95% of variance
pca = PCA(n_components=0.95)
X_reduced = pca.fit_transform(X)

# Explained variance
print(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)
# [0.72, 0.18] → First 2 components explain 90%
```

## Visualization

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_2d = pca.fit_transform(X)

plt.scatter(X_2d[:, 0], X_2d[:, 1], c=labels, cmap='viridis')
plt.xlabel('PC1')
plt.ylabel('PC2')
plt.title('PCA Visualization')
plt.show()
```

> 💡 **PCA is perfect for visualizing high-dimensional data!**

slides.title: Anomaly Detection
slides.content:
# Anomaly Detection 🚨

Find unusual data points!

## Isolation Forest

```python
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest

model = IsolationForest(
    contamination=0.1,  # Expected outlier percentage
    random_state=42
)

# -1 = outlier, 1 = normal
predictions = model.fit_predict(X)

# Get anomaly scores (lower = more anomalous)
scores = model.score_samples(X)
```

## One-Class SVM

```python
from sklearn.svm import OneClassSVM

model = OneClassSVM(
    kernel='rbf',
    nu=0.1  # Upper bound on outlier fraction
)

# -1 = outlier, 1 = normal
predictions = model.fit_predict(X)
```

## Using DBSCAN for Anomalies

```python
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

model = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=5)
labels = model.fit_predict(X)

# Points with label -1 are outliers!
anomalies = X[labels == -1]
```

## Applications

| Domain | Anomaly Type |
|--------|-------------|
| 💳 Finance | Fraudulent transactions |
| 🏭 Manufacturing | Defective products |
| 🔐 Security | Intrusion detection |
| 🏥 Healthcare | Unusual test results |

> 🎯 **Anomaly detection is key for fraud and security!**

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Excellent Work! 🎉

You've mastered Unsupervised Learning!

## Clustering
- ✅ **K-Means** - Fast, simple, spherical clusters
- ✅ **DBSCAN** - Arbitrary shapes, finds outliers
- ✅ **Hierarchical** - Dendrograms, small datasets
- ✅ Elbow method to find optimal K

## Dimensionality Reduction
- ✅ **PCA** - Linear, fast, interpretable
- ✅ Keep X% of variance OR N components
- ✅ Great for visualization

## Anomaly Detection
- ✅ **Isolation Forest** - Fast, scalable
- ✅ **One-Class SVM** - Boundary-based
- ✅ **DBSCAN** - Cluster-based outliers

## Quick Reference

```python
# Clustering
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X)

# Dimensionality Reduction
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_2d = pca.fit_transform(X)

# Anomaly Detection
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
if_model = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1)
anomalies = if_model.fit_predict(X)  # -1 = anomaly
```

> 🚀 **Next Steps:** Learn about Deep Learning!
